question: Which combination of aetiological factors is most strongly associated with squamous cell carcinoma of the maxillary sinus?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: EBV and salted fish consumption are strongly associated with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), not maxillary sinus SCC.
While tobacco and alcohol are major risk factors for most head and neck SCC, sinonasal SCC has additional and more specific occupational risk factors that are higher yield.

Correct. Occupational exposure to hardwood dust (furniture makers, carpenters) is a well-established risk factor for adenocarcinoma of the ethmoid sinus and SCC of the sinonasal tract. Nickel refining is a recognised risk factor for sinonasal SCC. These occupational associations are important for clinical history-taking.
HPV (especially HPV-16) is associated with oropharyngeal SCC. Betel nut is associated with oral cavity SCC. Neither is the primary aetiological driver for maxillary sinus SCC.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the aetiology of sinonasal malignancies. Hardwood dust exposure (ethmoid adenocarcinoma) and nickel refining (SCC) are the key occupational associations for sinonasal cancers, distinguishing them from NPC (EBV, salted fish) and oropharyngeal SCC (HPV).
Correct. Hardwood dust and nickel refining are the classic occupational risk factors for sinonasal malignancy. Always ask about occupation when a patient presents with unilateral sinonasal symptoms.
